On November 9, 2017, nine-year-old Dezde-zyer Mays was crossing Babbitt Road in Euclid, Ohio, on her way to the bus stop when a car hit her and drove away.

 The impact broke her neck, both legs and every bone in her face, knocked out her teeth and split her chin. She died in the hospital on November 21.

​At her sentencing on May 24, 2018, Mays's mother and great-aunt spoke about the little girl they lost and the pain her death left behind. Tidmore received an eight-year prison sentence. Ohio records now show her under state supervision, with October 5, 2026, listed as her expected release date. 

​Eight years cannot give a child her life back or undo what her family has endured. Does this sentence feel like justice?
